title: Read a two-way specification matrix
scenario: Corvani Alloy Lab has 28 invented inspection records. Each required energy depends on both Grade_code and Orientation, using the Matrix sheet. A blank grade and an unknown orientation are included so an incomplete lookup cannot silently select a default.

lesson.intro: A two-way lookup finds both the row and column of a value. Search grade labels vertically and orientation labels horizontally; use their positions inside INDEX.

functions.name: INDEX
functions.purpose: Return the value at a row and column position.
functions.arguments: array contains values; row_num selects its row and optional column_num selects its column.
functions.useCase: Select an item in a specification matrix.
functions.mistake: Row positions are relative to the selected array, not worksheet row numbers.

functions.name: MATCH
functions.purpose: Find the relative position of a value.
functions.arguments: lookup_value is the key; lookup_array is one row or column; use match_type 0 for exact matching.
functions.useCase: Find a row or column position for INDEX.
functions.mistake: Omitting 0 requests approximate matching, which has ordering requirements.

lesson.combine: Reuse IFERROR for Missing and IF for a training-only energy decision. Use exact MATCH for each dimension; matching only the grade can produce a plausible but wrong requirement.

tasks.prompt: Find the first record’s Grade_code position in Matrix!A2:A5.
Find the first record’s Orientation position within Matrix!B1:C1.
For the first six records, return their energy requirement in J from the two-dimensional matrix, or Missing for an absent grade/orientation.
For the first record, return Pass if Energy_J meets or exceeds its two-way requirement, otherwise Hold.

bonus.prompt: Return the difference between the first grade’s LPA and TWA requirements: LPA minus TWA.
